- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or shows sharp negative swings, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per day to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast to trend toward historical 30-day average.  
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days, model is lagging — apply early correction by 1–2% per day to catch momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00 → 1.00), model often misreads trend — use sentiment swing as signal to adjust forecast direction mid-horizon.
